title: Symmetry considerations in chirality-induced spin selectivity
abstract: The chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect, the coupling between structural chirality and electron spin polarization, has been experimentally observed across many diverse systems. However, despite extensive theoretical effort, a unified mechanistic understanding remains elusive. In this perspective, we demonstrate how some of the basic properties of the fascinating effects of CISS can be understood based on straightforward symmetry considerations commonly employed in fundamental particle physics. In particular, we show that CISS does not violate any fundamental symmetries including parity and time-reversal. By anchoring CISS within the universal language of symmetry, we offer a robust conceptual foundation for interpreting experiments and guiding future theoretical and experimental designs.
summary: This theoretical work re-examines the CISS effect by imposing fundamental symmetry constraints, arguing that the effect's description must incorporate chirality ($\chi$) to remain consistent with symmetries like parity and time-reversal. By framing CISS within the language of symmetry invariants, the authors provide a powerful conceptual framework for interpreting related quantum transport experiments.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a unified, fundamental understanding of the Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect by grounding its description in symmetry principles.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the CISS effect, when properly formulated using rotational invariants, does not violate fundamental symmetries like parity (P) or time-reversal (T).
method: The analysis relies on symmetry considerations (P, T) and the construction of rotational invariants to characterize the correlation between structural chirality ($\chi$) and spin/current polarization ($\vec{s} \cdot \vec{J}$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on the CISS effect in both dynamic (current-driven) and quasi-static (overlayer interaction) scenarios involving chiral materials.
key_observables: Spin polarization ($\vec{s} \cdot \vec{J}$) and the chirality-dependent correlation $\chi\vec{s} \cdot \vec{J}$.
important_parameters: Structural chirality ($\chi$), Parity (P), and Time-Reversal (T) symmetry operations.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the underlying physics can be robustly described by symmetry constraints, although the invariants do not yield a quantitative prediction of the magnitude.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate chirality as a pseudoscalar (e.g., screws, optical rotation) and summarize how various physical quantities transform under discrete symmetries (P, T).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the empirical correlation ($\vec{s} \cdot \vec{J}$), then showing its symmetry deficiencies, and finally proposing the symmetry-constrained invariant ($\chi\vec{s} \cdot \vec{J}$) to provide a robust conceptual foundation.
why_interesting: While the core topic is condensed matter spintronics, the rigorous application of fundamental symmetry principles (P, T) to constrain a complex quantum transport phenomenon is highly relevant to theoretical physics.
